prompt:
Use-case: background-extraction with careful hidden-edge reconstruction for a game construction layer.
Reference image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: a crop from our project-owned new Demacian town composition. Reference image 2 is the complete project-owned composition, used ONLY to keep the exact LOWER FRONTAL camera, depth, lighting and painted material family. Reference image 3 is the official Demacia emblem, used ONLY to redraw the correct winged-blade shape on existing small blue cloth when cloth is present; no imported original pixels.
Output ONE complete, isolated construction object with a genuinely transparent RGBA background, soft short alpha ground contact shadow, comfortable transparent margins, no background rectangle. Keep the exact architectural complex from the crop, NOT a redesigned replacement. Preserve its asymmetry, volumes, roof angles, weathered pale stone, muted blue-gray slate, restrained old gold, dark openings, upper-left light and richly textured original-Heroes-III painted/prerendered treatment. Low frontal perspective with natural depth, NOT a high isometric dollhouse, orthographic icon, glossy modern 3D or League splash illustration. Architectural shape must read compactly at the specified native size. Remove all sky, mountains, river, trees, shrubs, roads, cliffs, neighboring structures and urban scenery. Keep only the building's own very shallow base/threshold and indispensable attached architectural elements. Reconstruct any cropped/occluded roof or wall edges naturally. No people, captions, labels, text, UI, frame, checkerboard or baked opaque background. Do not turn a functional building into part of a larger town painting. Do not add new structures.

Target: Royal Blacksmith, the foreground L-shaped smithy in reference1. Retain the long low blue-slate main workshop, left attached timber lean-to, large arched front forge entrance, short smoking stone forge/chimney, restrained orange coals, exposed sidewheel/workstation and compact racks/anvils/tools. The pale training building at the TOP of reference1 is a NEIGHBOR: remove it completely. No river, steps leading out of frame, broad paving courtyard, cliff or vegetation. Complete the leftmost eave and building edges so none are cut off. This near-camera human-scale workshop is intentionally broad and large on screen; retain its lower front view and shallow visible roof. Final native footprint approximately250x123pixels; select bold door/roof/forge values rather than tiny added clutter. Preserve the workshop from the crop exactly.
